coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Creek Park
names: Mission Creek Park -- east reach (Pavilion to 4th St bridge)
record.summary: The stretch of landscaped park -- lawn, paths and trees -- between the already-tracked Mission Creek Park Pavilion and the 4th Street bridge, on Mission Creek's north/west bank; already built, per satellite imagery, and traced with the property owner's direct, iterative guidance after this project's own PDF-pixel transform repeatedly mis-located the stretch. No independently published source names, dates or definitively labels this specific segment.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- hand-traced from satellite imagery with the owner's direct, iterative guidance (not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team, and not derived from the PDF-pixel transform, which was unreliable for this specific stretch). Status 'complete' since the landscaping is clearly already built (lawn, paths, trees visible), not a future plan.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery (contextily/Esri World Imagery), guided step-by-step by the owner (who knows this stretch directly) rather than the PDF-pixel transform, which repeatedly mis-located this segment.

open_questions: No independently published source dates when this specific stretch was built; it was hand-traced from satellite imagery because it was visibly already landscaped, not because any source dated its construction.

This record's own digitization_method log says OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 both fall somewhere in this general stretch, per that log's reading of the Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update' -- but that deck's own extractable text only labels the whole wider park 'Mission Creek Park (P3)' and does not break out a separate P1 sub-area within this specific reach; which label (if either) applies to this exact segment, versus to the separately tracked Mission Creek Park record's own P1 (an amphitheater, per OCII's current open-space page), is not resolved.
Name/operator: presumed to be part of the same SF Recreation and Park Department-managed Mission Creek Park system as its neighbors, but not independently confirmed for this specific segment.

2026-09-22 pass, flagged for the owner rather than resolved: this record is currently classified 'Mission Bay South' (approximate_projects.csv) and its own sourcing leans on Mission Bay South's P1/P3 plan labels (see above). But this record's own coordinates sit at the same latitude as other already-tracked Mission Bay North records (The Beacon, Rich Sorro Commons), north of the core of the separately-tracked, South-side mission_bay_creek_park record. A landscape architecture firm's own project page (Munden Fry Landscape Associates, mflastudio.com/mission-creek-park-north) independently describes real, differently-numbered 'NP1 Mission Creek Park Promenade' and 'NP2 Mission Creek Park' parcels for Catellus, built 1999-2011, on Mission Creek's north bank -- a description (residential to the north, the creek and a houseboat community to the south) that matches this record's own traced bank. Whether this segment is actually part of Mission Bay North's NP1/NP2 system rather than South's P1/P3 is an open identity question bigger than a date, not resolved here -- flagged for a closer look, possibly including whether this record's site classification itself should change.
